record.original_question: Let Ω be a Polish space. We call a semigroup T = (T (t))t≥0 of contractions on Cb (Ω) a transition semigroup if (i) for every f ∈ Cb (E) we have T (t)f → T (s)f locally uniformly whenever t → s and (ii) for every t ≥ 0 and every uniformly bounded sequence (fn )n∈N ⊂ Cb (Ω) that converges locally uniformly to f , we have that T (t)fn converges locally uniformly to f . Is there a characterization of the generators of such a semigroup akin to the Lumer–Phillips theorem?

evidence.quote: Problem (Lumer–Phillips for transition semigroups). Let Ω be a Polish space. We call a semigroup T = (T (t))t≥0 of contractions on Cb (Ω) a transition semigroup if (i) for every f ∈ Cb (E) we have T (t)f → T (s)f locally uniformly whenever t → s and (ii) for every t ≥ 0 and every uniformly bounded sequence (fn )n∈N ⊂ Cb (Ω) that converges locally uniformly to f , we have that T (t)fn converges locally uniformly to f . Is there a characterization of the generators of such a semigroup akin to the Lumer–Phillips theorem?

artifact.status_search_result: Lumer–Phillips type generation theorems have recently been established in the broader framework of bi-continuous semigroups (e.g., Budde, 2022, arXiv:2202.10730 and 2206.00887), which include transition semigroups on $C_b(\Omega)$ as a key motivating example. Whether these results constitute a fully satisfactory Lumer–Phillips characterization specifically for transition semigroups in the locally-uniform-convergence sense described is not definitively settled by the search; the question appears to remain open or at best partially addressed.

status_evidence.title: A Lumer-Phillips type generation theorem for bi-continuous semigroups
status_evidence.snippet: Generators of τ-bi-continuous semigroups are characterized by dissipativity with respect to a directed system of seminorms and a range condition.
status_evidence.claim: A Lumer–Phillips style characterization exists for bi-continuous semigroups, a framework that includes transition semigroups on $C_b(\Omega)$ as a motivating example.

status_evidence.title: A note on the Lumer–Phillips theorem for bi-continuous semigroups
status_evidence.snippet: Note refining the Lumer–Phillips theorem in the bi-continuous setting.
status_evidence.claim: Further refinements of Lumer–Phillips for bi-continuous semigroups have been published, suggesting the topic is actively developing rather than fully closed.
